sources.quote: According to The Daily Beast’s analysis of Federal Election Commission filings, the 43 client PACs on the call center website have raised more than $140 million in the last two election cycles alone.
sources.searcher_note: Closest analog: a network of 43 cause-named PACs, all clients of one call center, $140M over two cycles, most of it spent on fundraising. Not the same 41-PAC set, and no share-to-politics figure.

sources.quote: The Law Enforcement for a Safer America PAC also reported nearly $1.6 million in payments to Public Support Services, all for “fundraising” services.
sources.searcher_note: Names sympathy-named PACs and a shared fundraising vendor (Public Support Services). Also flags 86 possible scam PACs in the 2022 cycle and covers the Piaro/Zeitlin indictments. Pattern coverage with a vendor angle.

sources.quote: Instead, their contributions end up with a super PAC, Law Enforcement for a Safer America, which has ties to a controversial union and spends the majority of its money on its own operating costs.
sources.searcher_note: A police-named super PAC that spends mostly on its own operating costs. May be one of the 41, but the lead's list wasn't available to check. The article adds that small-donor super PACs cost more to run, though this much is still unusual.

sources.quote: Zeitlin’s call center profited big from the donations, raking in about 90 percent of each dollar raised, while the rest was given to the respective PAC.
sources.searcher_note: Covers the Piaro PACs ($28M). The lead dropped two Piaro PACs from its count, so this is overlapping pattern coverage of the telemarketing-vendor scheme.

sources.outlet: Office of Sen. Richard Blumenthal (letter to FEC)
sources.quote: A recent New York Times investigation found one network of telemarketers had raised $89 million in political donations on behalf of law enforcement, firefighters, and veterans, but had only spent 1% on actual campaign activities and contributions.
sources.searcher_note: Senator's letter citing the NYT (the $89M network was nonprofits, not super PACs) and the $140M scam-PAC network. Pattern-level.

sources.quote: Scam PACs? Two Groups Claim To Support Vets And Cops While Blowing All Their Money On Administrative Fees.
sources.searcher_note: Blocked (403). Headline only. Per the search snippet, three UPS-Store-mailbox vendors took 89% of American Veterans Initiative money, a vendor-block pattern; not verified from the page.

notes: Heavy pattern coverage of scam PACs, 2020-2024: the Daily Beast 43-PAC/$140M network, OpenSecrets, CNN, Forbes, SDNY's Piaro/Zeitlin case, the Blumenthal letter, the Colorado SOS warning page. No source found builds the same set of 41 sympathy-named super PACs, the $181.5M total, the 4% or 12.5% share to politics, or the claim that a six-vendor phone/caging block is paid only by sympathy-named committees. Some named PACs (e.g. Law Enforcement for a Safer America) may overlap the 41; checking that needs the lead's list. The AP/Bangor Daily News story of 2024-07-02 ('Scam PACs' invoke veterans, police and politicians) redirected to a consent wall and couldn't be quoted. The DOJ SDNY release on Piaro/Zeitlin returned an empty page. The Colorado SOS page says 'most of your donation will support the PAC’s organizers and vendors'. Nothing after 2026-06-30 found.
